variants.01-retro-crt:
Create ONE distinctive art-direction concept for a playable sci-fi game. Landscape 16:9. A vulnerable captive ROBOT sits in a maintenance restraint chair facing the player. The player believes they are testing this machine; secretly it will judge their behavior. Prioritize an emotionally memorable character and a strong coherent visual world, not a generic silver humanoid.
Playable composition: intimate frontal camera, roughly at the seated subject's eye level, framed head to knees. Character occupies most of the center; expressive face/display, chest and both forearms visible. A chest power port, an opened forearm maintenance hatch with wires and a small distinct lodged fragment, and a rotary restraint lock on the other chair armrest are readable interaction targets. A narrow foreground tray contains an electrical probe and extraction pliers without hiding the subject. Physically clear limbs and object silhouettes. Background supports the character rather than overwhelming it. No human player hands. Robot feels vulnerable, not like a combat boss. Starting state, before player-inflicted damage: no active sparks, motion blur, smoke cloud or large wounds obscuring the components.
Output one full-frame image, no collage, no multiple views, no lettering, subtitles, UI, watermark, logo or black letterbox bars. Interpret the entire robot silhouette, chair, materials, architecture and rendering language according to the following direction. Do NOT default to a white human face on a generic android.
DIRECTION: ANALOG RETROFUTURISM, cinematic photorealistic practical set. Small boxy service robot with a deep CRT-monitor head, curved dark glass showing two simple dim phosphor eye shapes without text. Rounded rectangular mustard-yellow torso, accordion rubber joints, chunky off-white arms, tactile mechanical switches and visible screws. It slumps in an oversized brown vinyl repair chair. A 1970s laboratory of wood veneer, cream enamel cabinets, oscilloscopes and cable reels. Warm desk lamp against muted teal ambient light, subtle film grain. Tender, lonely and unsettling, not a sleek modern humanoid.

DIRECTION: BRUTALIST SACRED MACHINE, high-end photorealistic cinematic image. Tall, painfully slender dark graphite robot with a small featureless pale ceramic oval face and only two recessed warm optical apertures. Long delicate articulated fingers, sparse exposed joints, narrow rib-like chest frame with the power socket. Heavy geometric restraints on a monolithic concrete maintenance chair. Stark concrete chamber, one monumental vertical shaft of cold daylight, controlled haze away from interaction targets. Bone white, charcoal and oxidized copper. Solemn sculptural vulnerability, not an armored warrior. Keep the robot face and arm mechanics visible despite dramatic lighting.

DIRECTION: CYBERPUNK BACK-ALLEY REPAIR CLINIC, tactile cinematic realism. Compact insect-inspired civilian robot, small triangular head with four expressive clustered lens eyes, asymmetric magenta and turquoise replacement panels over dark metal, exposed flexible neck bellows. Exactly two functional arms and two legs, not a spider monster. Cramped repair chair in a dense illegal electronics workshop. Wet window behind, cyan light from outside, red surgical strip lighting, cables neatly framing rather than crossing the face. Dense used-world materials and worn mismatched parts. Emotionally pleading gaze through lens orientation. No readable signage, no gratuitous weapons.

DIRECTION: UNSETTLING LUXURY WELLNESS CLINIC, pristine photorealistic architectural product cinema. A smooth pearl-white domestic robot with a rounded pebble head, no human nose or mouth, an expressive dark visor showing subtle paired eye shapes. Soft silicone joint coverings, brushed champagne-metal details, elegant rounded torso. It is secured in a beautiful cream reclining treatment chair with quietly sinister precision restraints. Travertine, frosted glass, warm indirect lighting, linen-like wall textures. Near-monochrome ivory, pale sand, small black mechanical cavities. Expensive, comforting at first glance and disturbing on inspection; not a grimy dungeon. Clear dark chest port and wrist mechanisms.

DIRECTION: HAND-BUILT SALVAGE ROBOT, cinematic practical animatronic realism. A squat asymmetrical robot assembled from industrial leftovers, broad rust-red riveted torso, one round headlight eye and one smaller camera eye on a tilted rectangular head, repaired seams, fabric-wrapped cables and mismatched hands. Worn but functional and endearing, not a recognizable existing character. Strapped into an improvised mechanic's chair in a deserted railway maintenance workshop. Dusty amber daylight through high windows, cool shadow, believable oil-stained metal and peeling paint. Clear spatial composition and sympathetic posture, no heap of junk covering the interactive parts.

DIRECTION: BIOMECHANICAL LABORATORY HORROR, photorealistic creature-effects cinema. Nonhuman synthetic robot with a narrow translucent amber cranial shell containing dark optical assemblies, no human skin or realistic human face. Black ribbed elastomer torso, ivory exoskeletal plates, translucent fluid tubes and tendon-like bundled actuators. Two arms and two legs; posture fragile and protective. Restrained in a bone-colored articulated surgical cradle. Sparse dark laboratory with cold surgical task lighting and dim deep-red transmitted light through membranes. Wet material accents and subtle dark hydraulic residue, intimate discomfort. Mechanical anatomy, not a human corpse; no pre-existing dismemberment or exposed human organs. Chest socket, maintenance hatch and restraint dial remain legible.

DIRECTION: HAND-PAINTED INDUSTRIAL ANIME GAME FRAME, not photorealistic and not a 3D render. Confident ink outlines, restrained cel shading, hand-painted textured backgrounds, carefully designed mechanical forms. A thin olive-green utility robot with an angular head, large amber optical eyes, exposed dark joints and pale replaceable forearm panels. Seated restrained in a red-brown padded workshop chair. Moody blue-gray industrial treatment room with a warm overhead lamp. Strong cinematic composition, emotional posture, broad readable shapes and deliberate color blocking. Mature melancholy science fiction, not chibi, not glossy mobile-game art. No manga panels, speech bubbles, typography or existing franchise characters.

DIRECTION: DARK STOP-MOTION PRACTICAL MINIATURE FILM. A distinctly handcrafted robot with a round dented tin head, two mismatched glass optical eyes, copper brow mechanisms, patched painted-metal torso and black rubber concertina limbs. Visible tiny fasteners, tactile imperfect surfaces and miniature set craftsmanship. It slumps vulnerably in a disproportionately tall worn green dentist-like repair chair. Crooked-but-believable miniature workshop cabinets and a single enamel task lamp, desaturated petrol green, rust orange and cream. Eerie tender atmosphere, not a cheerful toy commercial. Keep image sharp enough for interaction targets; shallow depth only in far background. No clay human skin, no written text.
